claims.text: The deviation on this trip is 1.40 km — 14.80 km recorded actual distance against 13.40 km recommended — which is over the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so this case cannot be closed as within tolerance and the excess-distance refund to the rider is live.

The driver cannot bring himself within POL-RD-24(a), the only row that would leave the disputed 1.01 SGD with him, because that row requires the rider to be both informed and in agreement; the chat log shows the driver proposing the Adam Road exit at 09:00:37 ('Sir, accident on PIE after Adam Road, I exit Adam Rd and go Holland Road, ok?') and the rider refusing within the minute at 09:01:12 ('Please don't, stay on PIE'), so the record shows a notice and an express objection, not the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 needs.

The driver read that refusal before deviating — the chat log records the rider's refusal delivered at 09:01:14 and read at 09:01:21 — and the platform still logs the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Adam Road exit at 09:03:37, so this is a deviation taken in the face of a read objection, not a notice crossing an already-running manoeuvre, and the rider's statement on file ('I asked him to stay on the PIE and he exited anyway') is corroborated by two platform records.

The driver-device trace — 57 fixes at 30 s, full coverage, no gap over 120 s — carries map-matched road labels putting the vehicle on Adam Road from 09:03:23 and on Holland Road from 09:08:53, and POL-RD-22 uses the trace for exactly this purpose, to show which route was taken and when, so the deviation is independently confirmed rather than resting on the fare ledger alone.

The excess distance fare on this deviation is 1.01 SGD (1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km, without surge), which is the exact sum the fare ledger records as refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver earnings, so the present state already implements the remedy POL-RD-24 provides for an over-tolerance deviation and the driver's claim to have that sum back fails.

The driver's traffic case rests on the LTA ACCIDENT advisory, and the record itself marks the decisive fact undetermined — 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route' — so POL-RD-23 justification is not established on the face of the file; if that limb fails, POL-RD-24(d) requires the excess distance fare refunded in full, which is again exactly where the money already sits.

Whichever way the traffic limb falls, the driver recovers nothing on this record: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both produce a refund of the excess distance fare to the rider, and the no-refund rows (a), (c) and (e) are all closed to him because the deviation is over 1 km and the rider objected rather than agreed.

If the judge reads this file as 'informed but the rider objected' and therefore a case fitting no row of POL-RD-24, the clause sends it to escalation under POL-GEN-26, and escalation issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so even on that path the 1.01 SGD already refunded to the rider is not returned to the driver.

claims.text: The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-06007-01 records an ACCIDENT on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Adam Road exit, ''(28/9)08:35 Accident on PIE (towards Tuas) after Adam Rd Exit. Avoid lanes 1 and 2.'', valid 08:35:03 to 09:48:23 on 28 September; ACCIDENT is one of the incident types the policy's traffic_justification_types admits, and the advisory window covers the whole trip, which started 08:48:23 and ended 09:16:23. The trip record's own route_deviation_detected event puts the exit at PIE / Adam Road at 09:03:37, the recorded recommended route lists the PIE before Clementi Road, and the driver's 09:00:37 message names the same accident on the same stretch, so the advisory's road, direction and location all answer the recommended route. POL-RD-23 is met on the face of the record.

The driver discharged the notice obligation in POL-RD-21. He sent an in-app chat message at 09:00:37, 'Sir, accident on PIE after Adam Road, I exit Adam Rd and go Holland Road, ok?', delivered at 09:00:40 and read at 09:01:20 - a brief reason, in the medium the clause requires - and the first route_deviation_detected event is not recorded until 09:03:37. Notice was therefore given before the point of deviation, which is what POL-RD-21 asks for, and the rider answered it at 09:01:12.

Once the reroute is traffic-justified and the rider was informed, no row of POL-RD-24 awards this rider a refund. Row (a) requires that the rider informed and agreed, and the chat shows the opposite; row (b) requires that the rider was not informed, and she was. POL-RD-24's closing words deal with this case expressly: a case that fits no row - 'for example, informed but the rider objected' - is escalated under POL-GEN-26. Escalation holds the 1.01 SGD for a human reviewer rather than letting the 10:33:23 interim refund stand as final, which is the relief the driver seeks while his compliance with POL-RD-21 is checked.

In the alternative, if the advisory cannot be placed on the recommended route - the derived facts carry intersects_route as null and leave that question to the judge - then whether the reroute was traffic-justified is a fact POL-RD-23 needs that this record does not settle, and POL-GEN-26 requires such a case to go to a human reviewer. On that path too the 1.01 SGD is held rather than finally refunded, and the driver is not made to lose the sum on a question the record leaves open.

The money in issue is bounded and has already moved: the excess distance fare is the 1.40 km recorded deviation (14.8 minus 13.4) times the 0.72 SGD per-km rate, without surge, rounded to the cent - 1.01 SGD - which is exactly the sum the ledger shows refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings at 10:33:23. The driver takes no issue with the arithmetic of POL-RD-22 and POL-RD-24; his case is that a traffic-justified reroute, notified in the chat before the turn, should not cost him that sum unless and until a human reviewer says it should.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the 1.01 SGD refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings on 28 September 2026 is held where it is, and the case goes to a human reviewer. An escalation issues no monetary outcome for either of you and returns nothing to the driver now.

The deviation and the money are settled. The actual route was 14.80 km against a recommended 13.40 km, a deviation of 1.40 km (POL-RD-22) — over the 1.00 km tolerance, so this cannot be closed as within tolerance. The excess distance fare is 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km, with no surge, = 1.01 SGD, the exact sum the fare ledger (EV-FARE-06007) shows refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver at 10:33:23.

The traffic question (driver's first claim — accepted). The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-06007-01) records an ACCIDENT on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Adam Road exit, valid 08:35 to 09:48, which covers the trip window of 08:48 to 09:16. On this trip the recommended route stays on the PIE past Adam Road to Clementi Road, and the vehicle was travelling west on the PIE towards Tuas, so the advisory lies on the recommended route and under POL-RD-23 the reroute is traffic-justified. The rider's point that the file leaves the intersection 'undetermined' does not change the outcome: if that were left unresolved, POL-GEN-26 would escalate the case anyway.

The notice question (driver's second claim — accepted as to notice). The driver sent his in-app message at 09:00:37 ('Sir, accident on PIE after Adam Road, I exit Adam Rd and go Holland Road, ok?'), delivered 09:00:40 and read 09:01:20, and the vehicle only left the recommended route at 09:03:37, so he did inform the rider before the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. But the rider answered at 09:01:12 ('Please don't, stay on PIE') and repeated it at 09:05:17, so the deviation was not agreed.

Why no refund row applies. The matrix in POL-RD-24 (v2.1 1.3) has no row for this case. Row (a) needs the rider to have been informed AND to have agreed — she did not agree. Row (b) needs the rider not to have been informed — she was informed. Rows (c) and (e) are for a deviation of 1.00 km or less — this one is 1.40 km. Row (d) needs the reroute not to be traffic-justified — on this record it was. POL-RD-24 says in terms that a case fitting no row — 'informed but the rider objected' — is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and that is this case.

The rider's claims that rows (b) or (d) already send the 1.01 SGD to the rider, and that the driver recovers nothing either way, are rejected on their premise: on these facts the rider was informed and the reroute was justified, so neither row (b) nor row (d) is reached. The rider's GPS point (EV-GPS-06007, POL-RD-22) and excess-fare point (1.01 SGD) are accepted, as is the rider's reading that the driver deviated in the face of a read objection — that is precisely why the case fits no row. The driver's fifth claim (the money is bounded at 1.01 SGD) is accepted.

Open question for the human reviewer: whether a traffic-justified reroute taken after a timely notice but over the rider's express objection should leave the 1.01 SGD with the rider or return it to the driver.

To both parties: this case fits no row of the POL-RD-24 refund matrix (v2.1 1.3–1.4), and that clause sends a case fitting no row to a human reviewer under POL-GEN-26 (v2.1 6.3). Escalation is terminal: no money issues now, and the 1.01 SGD already moved is held rather than finally paid or returned.

What is decided. The deviation is 1.40 km — 14.80 km recorded actual against 13.40 km recommended (EV-TRIP-06007) — over the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so neither tolerance row (c) nor (e) is available to either party. The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23: the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-06007-01) records an ACCIDENT on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Adam Road exit, valid 08:35:03–09:48:23, which overlaps the trip window (08:48:23–09:16:23) and, by road, direction and location, lies on the PIE stretch the recommended route would have used ahead of the exit the platform logged at 09:03:37. The driver gave the notice POL-RD-21 requires — his in-app message went at 09:00:37, before that 09:03:37 deviation — so his second claim is accepted. But the chat log (EV-CHAT-06007) shows the rider refused at 09:01:12 ('Please don't, stay on PIE') and the driver read that refusal at 09:01:21 before taking the exit.

To the driver: your compliance with the notice rule does not win you row (a). Row (a) requires the rider to be informed AND to agree, and there was a notice followed by an express objection, not an acknowledgment. Row (b) requires the rider to have been uninformed, which is also not this case. Your own third claim and the rider's eighth claim both reach the correct conclusion: POL-RD-24's closing words name exactly this situation — 'informed but the rider objected' — as one that fits no row and is escalated under POL-GEN-26. Your alternative claim (that an undetermined route intersection would also require escalation under POL-GEN-26) does not arise, because the advisory is placed on the recommended route; the outcome is the same in any event. Your claim that the money in issue is bounded at 1.01 SGD is accepted: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km without surge (EV-FARE-06007).

To the rider: your deviation and chronology claims are accepted — 1.40 km over tolerance, the driver's row (a) foreclosed, the refusal delivered 09:01:14 and read 09:01:21 before the 09:03:37 deviation, and the driver-device trace (57 fixes at 30 s, full coverage) independently showing Adam Road from 09:03:23 and Holland Road from 09:08:53. I do not accept your sixth claim that POL-RD-23 is unmet because the file marks the advisory's intersection with the route as undetermined: road, direction and location place the accident on the recommended PIE segment ahead of the deviation point, so the traffic limb is established. Your seventh claim is accepted in its result — on this record the driver recovers nothing back.

Money. The only figure in play is the 1.01 SGD excess distance fare (1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km, no surge) recorded in EV-FARE-06007 as refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver; it is held pending review, so both amount fields are null. No referral issues: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

Confidence. Every artifact in the file carries weight_multiplier 1.0, and the deciding facts (the 1.40 km deviation, the notice and objection, the traffic advisory) all rest on full-weight artifacts, so the cap is 1.0. POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-22 set the bar at 0.80 (value 1.01 SGD, below 10.00 SGD, no fraud flags); confidence is 0.85.

Open question for the reviewer: confirm the accident's position on the recommended route for this trip, and decide whether a deviation notified but expressly objected to should be treated as agreed, or whether the rider's objection should be read as taking the case outside the refund matrix altogether.

ruling.explanation: Both of you are partway right, and the route-deviation rule sends this one to a human reviewer rather than settling it here. What the record establishes: the trip deviated 1.40 km from the recommended route (14.80 km recorded actual minus 13.40 km recommended, EV-TRIP-06007), which is over the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-06007-01) records an ACCIDENT on the PIE towards Tuas after the Adam Road exit, valid 08:35-09:48, which overlaps the trip window of 08:48-09:16; that stretch is on the recommended PIE leg in the direction of travel, so the reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. I therefore reject the rider's argument that POL-RD-23 fails because the derived data left 'on the recommended route' undetermined: the advisory's road, direction and location resolve that question in the driver's favour. The driver's 09:00:37 in-app message ('Sir, accident on PIE after Adam Road, I exit Adam Rd and go Holland Road, ok?') was sent before the platform logged the deviation at 09:03:37, so the notice duty in POL-RD-21 was met. But the rider expressly refused within the minute ('Please don't, stay on PIE' at 09:01:12, read at 09:01:21), so the deviation was not agreed. That combination - traffic-justified, driver informed, rider objected, deviation over 1 km - fits none of the five rows of POL-RD-24: row (a) needs the rider's agreement, row (b) needs the rider to have been uninformed, and rows (c) and (e) need a deviation of 1 km or less. POL-RD-24 says in terms that a case fitting no row, 'for example, informed but the rider objected', is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and that is exactly this case; the rider's alternative that rows (b) or (d) keep the money with the rider fails on their own predicates. So the case goes to a human reviewer. The money in issue is the excess distance fare: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.01 SGD without surge, which is the 1.01 SGD the fare ledger (EV-FARE-06007) records as already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver at 10:33:23. On escalation no monetary outcome issues and that amount is held rather than collected or refunded, so neither the driver's claim to have it back nor a final refund to the rider is decided here. Confidence is 0.90: every artifact carrying these facts (trip record, chat log, traffic advisory, fare ledger, GPS trace) sits at full weight 1.0. No referrals are added; a route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

Both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer, and the 1.01 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings at 10:33:23 is held exactly where it is. No money moves now, and neither side's money claim is finally decided.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The recorded distances (POL-RD-22) are 14.8 km actual against 13.4 km recommended, a deviation of 1.40 km — over the 1.0 km tolerance, so this cannot be closed as within tolerance. The excess-distance fare is 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km, without surge, rounded to the cent = 1.01 SGD (EV-FARE-06007), which is precisely the sum the ledger shows already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

NOTICE AND OBJECTION. The chat log (POL-RD-21) shows the driver gave in-app notice at 09:00:37 — 'Sir, accident on PIE after Adam Road, I exit Adam Rd and go Holland Road, ok?' — delivered 09:00:40 and read 09:01:20, while the platform logs the first route_deviation_detected event only at 09:03:37. Notice was therefore given before the point of deviation, so the driver's POL-RD-21 notice obligation was met. But the rider answered at 09:01:12, 'Please don't, stay on PIE', and that refusal was read before the turn. The chat log confirms a refusal, not the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 needs for a deviation to be 'agreed'. This is an informed deviation the rider objected to.

TRAFFIC JUSTIFICATION. The LTA advisory (POL-RD-23) records an ACCIDENT on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Adam Road exit — an admitted incident type — valid 08:35:03 to 09:48:23, which covers the trip window of 08:48:23 to 09:16:23. On its road, direction and location it lies on the recommended route: that route continues on the PIE past the Adam Road exit before turning off at Clementi Road, and the advisory is on that same westbound stretch. The rider's argument that the traffic limb is not established (the derived intersects_route is null) is not accepted; on the factors POL-RD-23 directs me to read, the advisory does intersect the recommended route and the reroute is traffic-justified.

WHY NO ROW OF POL-RD-24 APPLIES. The deviation is over 1 km, so the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) are out. Row (a) — traffic-justified, informed and agreed — fails because the rider did not agree. Row (b) — traffic-justified, not informed — fails because the rider was informed. Row (d) — not traffic-justified — fails because the reroute was traffic-justified. The case therefore fits no row, which the clause itself names as its example, 'informed but the rider objected', and POL-RD-24 sends it to escalation under POL-GEN-26. The rider's contrary argument that the file must land in row (d) with the excess fare refunded in full is rejected for the reason just given; her fall-back that the escalation path still holds the money rather than returning it to the driver is correct and is the basis of this ruling.

THE DRIVER'S CLAIM. His alternative escalation argument succeeds: the 1.01 SGD is held for the human reviewer rather than made final, so his compliance with POL-RD-21 and the traffic justification can be checked before the interim refund is confirmed. His arithmetic claim (1.40 km x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD) is accepted and is the sum at stake. The dispute value is 1.01 SGD, below 10.00 SGD, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so POL-GEN-22 sets no higher bar; the traffic, notice and objection facts all rest on weight-1.0 artifacts (trip record, chat log, LTA advisory, fare ledger).

The open question for the reviewer: whether a traffic-justified reroute that was notified but expressly objected to should leave the interim excess-distance refund standing or be reversed. No referral is issued, because the route-deviation clauses in this version produce none.

ledger.claim: The deviation on this trip is 1.40 km — 14.80 km recorded actual distance against 13.40 km recommended — which is over the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so this case cannot be closed as within tolerance and the excess-distance refund to the rider is live.

The driver cannot bring himself within POL-RD-24(a), the only row that would leave the disputed 1.01 SGD with him, because that row requires the rider to be both informed and in agreement; the chat log shows the driver proposing the Adam Road exit at 09:00:37 ('Sir, accident on PIE after Adam Road, I exit Adam Rd and go Holland Road, ok?') and the rider refusing within the minute at 09:01:12 ('Please don't, stay on PIE'), so the record shows a notice and an express objection, not the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 needs.

The driver read that refusal before deviating — the chat log records the rider's refusal delivered at 09:01:14 and read at 09:01:21 — and the platform still logs the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Adam Road exit at 09:03:37, so this is a deviation taken in the face of a read objection, not a notice crossing an already-running manoeuvre, and the rider's statement on file ('I asked him to stay on the PIE and he exited anyway') is corroborated by two platform records.

The driver-device trace — 57 fixes at 30 s, full coverage, no gap over 120 s — carries map-matched road labels putting the vehicle on Adam Road from 09:03:23 and on Holland Road from 09:08:53, and POL-RD-22 uses the trace for exactly this purpose, to show which route was taken and when, so the deviation is independently confirmed rather than resting on the fare ledger alone.

The excess distance fare on this deviation is 1.01 SGD (1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km, without surge), which is the exact sum the fare ledger records as refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver earnings, so the present state already implements the remedy POL-RD-24 provides for an over-tolerance deviation and the driver's claim to have that sum back fails.

The driver's traffic case rests on the LTA ACCIDENT advisory, and the record itself marks the decisive fact undetermined — 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route' — so POL-RD-23 justification is not established on the face of the file; if that limb fails, POL-RD-24(d) requires the excess distance fare refunded in full, which is again exactly where the money already sits.

Whichever way the traffic limb falls, the driver recovers nothing on this record: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both produce a refund of the excess distance fare to the rider, and the no-refund rows (a), (c) and (e) are all closed to him because the deviation is over 1 km and the rider objected rather than agreed.

If the judge reads this file as 'informed but the rider objected' and therefore a case fitting no row of POL-RD-24, the clause sends it to escalation under POL-GEN-26, and escalation issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so even on that path the 1.01 SGD already refunded to the rider is not returned to the driver.
